Hi Sarah — thanks, this is great. Attaching a draft runbook (CS_PrePay_Schedule_v1.xlsx) that lays out the recommended flow. High level answers inline:  

- Invoice sequencing: Redwood can support either a single upfront invoice or monthly invoices. For committed spend we typically offer: (a) Upfront invoice for the committed amount (preferred by finance for simplicity); or (b) Monthly invoicing with an automated drawdown reconciliation file. For your PO I recommend monthly invoices tied to drawdowns so the ledger matches consumption. If you prefer upfront we can mark it as prepaid and amortize.

- Drawdown triggers: Proposed windows: 01–07 UTC each month for weekly/automated sweep (monthly netting at 00:00 UTC on the 8th). If usage crosses a 20% threshold mid-month we can trigger an interim drawdown. Details in tab "Windows & Thresholds" in the attachment.

- VAT/evidence: For US entities no VAT; for EU entities we need either (a) valid VAT registration & certificate per country (preferred) or (b) signed confirmation to use reverse-charge where applicable. Looping in Kimberly for definitive routing.

- Escrow vs sweep: We can accept a custodial escrow release for the first tranche. Our standard is a monthly sweep to Redwood's settlement account (details in the runbook). If escrow is required we will provide the escrow routing and acceptance checklist.

Next steps: I will loop in our tax and ledger owners (cc'ed) to confirm the VAT and ledger mapping. I will also send a short one-page runbook and the first-month invoice sample.

Marissa, team — quick VAT / tax routing note:  

- US: no VAT. Invoice CloudScale US entity directly (no VAT) — use their PO as reference.
- EU: Redwood accepts either (A) full copy of country VAT certificate(s) per EU entity (we prefer a single zip with one cert per country) OR (B) signed buyer declaration for reverse-charge per EU law where buyer is VAT-registered (we cannot accept a unilateral reverse-charge without evidence).
- If CloudScale wants to apply reverse-charge, they must supply: VAT registration number + signed reconciliation statement. Otherwise we will invoice with VAT where required and provide VAT lines on the invoice.

Escrow / sweep implications: Escrow is fine for the first tranche. For escrow we need: escrow agreement (counter-signed), beneficiary wiring, and a release schedule. If we move to monthly sweep we will provide Redwood settlement account details and a remittance template.

Attachments for CloudScale: VAT_Certificates.zip (placeholder) — ask them to provide per-country certs.

I'll add the tax-code mappings to the runbook and provide the list of invoice tax lines (tax_code_us, tax_code_eu_vat). Priyom — I will send the tax mapping sheet to you after you confirm the ledger tags.

Thanks,
